what: Brookfield Asset Management invests other people's money in real assets: infrastructure, renewable power, property, private equity and credit. It manages over a trillion dollars and earns fees for doing so.
customers: More than 2,400 institutional clients including pension funds, sovereign wealth funds, insurers and endowments.
money: management fees on committed capital, plus performance fees
moat: A century of operating experience in physical assets, which lets it buy and run infrastructure and property that financial buyers cannot manage themselves.
risks: Higher interest rates reduce the value of long-lived infrastructure and property
Fundraising slows when investors are already heavily committed to private assets
Performance fees are unpredictable and depend on exits
It is closely tied to Brookfield Corporation, which complicates the ownership structure
opportunities: Fee-bearing capital has been growing steadily and fees are paid on committed, not invested, money
Energy transition and data centre infrastructure need exactly the capital it raises
It carries effectively no debt at the manager level and pays out most of its earnings
watch: Fee-bearing capital and fee-related earnings, which are the recurring part.
